title: Houston strip-center retail: JADE retrofit
climate: Houston, TX: hot and humid. Plenty of 65-70°F days at 90%+ RH.
spec: Engineer's spec: differential enthalpy economizer control.
Occupied minimum OA damper position: 15% (3.2 V).
Mixed air low limit 45°F, damper to closed on freeze protection.
Occupancy from the BAS through the OCC input.
Prove full actuator stroke and Y1 staging at checkout.

consequences.strategy: 30 days later: humidity complaints. Dry bulb says 68°F air is free cooling, so the JADE pulls in 95% RH air all morning. Store's clammy, mold on the ceiling tile at the entrance. Callback.
consequences.MIN POS: 30 days later: wrong ventilation. Too high = coil overloaded and bills up in August; too low = stale air and an IAQ complaint.
consequences.MA LO SET: 30 days later: a cold front comes through and the freeze limit doesn't protect the coil the way the engineer intended.
consequences.FREEZE POS: 30 days later: a January cold snap. Damper holds open on freeze protection and the coil sees sub-freezing air.
consequences.OCC: 30 days later: the damper stays at min position all night with the store empty. Wasted energy, and the BAS tech calls you.
consequences.checkout: You never proved the actuator strokes. Two weeks later the owner finds the damper was stuck at closed the whole time.

note: Job specs are training values written to exercise the controller, not code-required values.
